data.jobspec:
#!/bin/sh
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE:
#   The Slurm script uses a shell variable in a directive (`-n ${NP}`), which is not valid in Flux batch directives.
#   Provide the total task count as the first argument when running this script.
#
# Run with:
#   flux batch <this_script> -- <NTASKS>

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=perf_cylinder
#   --partition=thin
#   --time=2-00:00:00
#   -n ${NP}
#   -o stdout-benchmark/slurm-%j-%4t-%n.out
#   -e stdout-benchmark/slurm-%j-%4t-%n.err

#flux: --job-name=perf_cylinder
#flux: -N 1
#flux: --time-limit=48h

# Omitted Slurm option: -n ${NP}
# Flux batch directives must be static; no portable variable expansion.
# Performance implication: if you do not pass/allocate the intended task count externally, the job may run with too few resources or oversubscribe.

# Omitted Slurm option: --partition=thin
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different limits/priority or on different hardware (or be rejected by policy).

# Omitted Slurm options: -o/-e with %j/%t/%n tokens
# Slurm token expansion is not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

NTASKS=$1
if [ -z "$NTASKS" ]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <NTASKS>" >&2
  exit 2
fi

source ../compile/modules_snellius.sh
export CASE_ID=1
echo "Starting case: $CASE_ID"

# Slurm used mpiexecjl; under Flux, use flux-run to launch ranks.
flux run -n "$NTASKS" -c 1 mpiexecjl --project=../ -n "$NTASKS" \
  julia -J ../PerforatedCylinder_parallel.so -O3 --check-bounds=no -e 'include("run_case_benchmark.jl")'

reasons: The resource section does not request any task/rank count (no `#flux: -n ...`), even though the job is intended to run MPI across a user-specified number of tasks; the allocation may default to a single task and not match the intended parallel resources.

The original Slurm job specified a partition (`--partition=thin`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition selection; on sites where this affects eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.
